label: sec:initialization_likelihood
claim: The complete moving-average normalization used for the multiplicative polynomial is D_reg(theta) D_seas(Theta) [R(theta, Theta; s)^2]^(-1/T), with R the resultant of the reversed regular and the seasonal MA polynomials.
evidence: No revision of the package implements the resultant factor: at 14dd581 (and at aa68d57, 3d7f883 and the current source) the Gaussian MA factor is prod_j (1 - kappa_j^2)^(-j/T) times prod_w (1 - kappa_w^2)^(-s w/T) only (src/models/sarima.jl, MA block of the :penalized/:innovations MSE objective). A cross term was tested in August 2026 in uncommitted source states and not adopted (Table S8, arm B). The identity of the equation itself holds: verification/ma_normalization/check_ma_normalization.py shows numerically that the complete multiplicative factor equals D_reg D_seas R^-2 (to 4e-14 in log), so the package's objective omits [R^2]^(-1/T), a factor between 0.987 and 1.010 at T = 200 over random invertible draws. Measured on the package (verification/ma_normalization/package_factor.jl, at 14dd581 and 21903b5): the factor applied equals D_reg D_seas to eight decimals, for both seasonal specifications.

label: sec:initialization_likelihood
claim: For the additive seasonal specification the normalization is a function of the complete MA polynomial 1 + sum theta_j B^j + sum Theta_w B^(sw).
evidence: The package applies the same separate regular and seasonal factors whatever the seasonal specification; it does not compute the reflection coordinates of the complete additive polynomial (the omitted factor is between 0.994 and 1.039 at T = 200 over random invertible draws; verification/ma_normalization/check_ma_normalization.py).
